text:
mika: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change in d3f4c2a, we've got a reproducible 12-18% P99 tail increase on the small-batcher path. nsys traces attached.
raj: ack, can you paste the nsys time range you used?
mika: full request span, 0:00:00.000 - 0:00:02.500. baseline (before change) trace is here: s3://redwood-traces/2026-03/selector-baseline.nsys, new trace: s3://redwood-traces/2026-03/selector-post.nsys
perf-bot: Automated perf summary: baseline P99=142ms, post-change P99=168ms (+18.3%). Hotspots: kernel 'kv_read_batch' increased self-time 3.8x; 'prefetch_dispatch' shows more serialization.
anya: interesting — did the selector start favoring the smaller kernel variant on longer sequences? that could increase contention in the kv layer.
mika: yes, selector config moved threshold from 128->96 tokens for small-kernel to reduce startup cost. suspect it increases number of small-kernel invocations which do more KV reads.
raj: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet from perfetto? small excerpt helps.
mika: sure, pasted snippet: ```
# perfetto slice
0.230s - 0.260s : small_kernel (stream 3)
0.260s - 0.270s : kv_read_batch (stream 2)
0.270s - 0.300s : small_kernel (stream 3)
0.300s - 0.340s : kv_read_batch (stream 2)
```
sam: that looks like kv_read_batch is being invoked between each small kernel call instead of being overlapped. previously we overlapped kv reads with compute.
infra-bot: note — GPU occupancy decreased by ~6% in post-change trace. memory copies per-request also up.
lucy: did we change prefetch window or batcher handshake? I remember a tweak in the continuous-batcher to prefer earlier handoff.
mika: correct, belt-queue handshake change in 7a9b11d to reduce request queue latency. probably combined effect.
raj: plan: 1) run targeted nvprof on kv_read_batch to see memcpy vs kernel time, 2) revert selector threshold in a feature branch to confirm impact, 3) git-bisect if needed.
anya: I'd add a perfetto flame compare of baseline vs post to show overlap loss. I can run that.
perf-bot: nvprof suggestion: use "nvprof --kernels kv_read_batch --analysis-metrics" and capture memcpy metrics (+ API calls).
sam: I'll try a quick revert locally: checkout -b revert-selector-96 && reset to d3f4c2a~1 then run the small-batcher harness.
mika: running bisect now: git bisect start -- good d3f4c2a~1 bad d3f4c2a. first run shows no regression if I also revert belt-queue handshake — suggests interaction.
raj: that points to a coupling issue. can we instrument kv cache to emit micro-traces of read latency and hits for each kernel variant?
anya: yes — add lightweight counters in kv cache hot path (atomic++ per-invocation, and histogram every 10k requests). we can collect with existing stats endpoint.
infra-bot: FYI — I scheduled a 2-hour reserved test on dedicated pool-3 for 03/18 16:00 UTC to reproduce at scale.
lucy: good. also add a test that forces continuous batching to prefer bigger handoffs to compare.
sam: quick note: I ran nvprof; kv_read_batch shows 42% of time spent on cudaMemcpyAsync in post-change trace vs 12% baseline. attaching short log excerpt: ```
[post] memcpy total: 24.1ms / kernel time 33.2ms
[base] memcpy total: 6.8ms / kernel time 47.5ms
```
mika: that's huge — suggests we lost caching/coalescing of batched reads.
raj: next steps: (a) add coalescing check in kv_read_batch to combine adjacent tiny reads, (b) reproduce with selector threshold reverted and handshake change toggled individually, (c) perfetto flame compare for overlap loss. assign: anya (perfetto), sam (revert+nvprof), mika (kv instrumentation), raj (coalescing patch).
anya: I'll upload flame compare and a short GIF to the trace ticket once done.
perf-bot: regression ticket created: PERF-7689, linked traces and nvprof logs.
mika: thanks — keep updates here. if anything shows it's purely the selector, we'll roll it back; if it's interaction, need a short-term mitigation (tweak handshake back + small patch to coalesce reads). :thumbsup:
raj: adding note — consider a defensive fallback in kernel-selector to detect high memcpy ratio and prefer the other variant automatically. low-risk short-term fix.
lucy: +1 on fallback heuristic. also flagging for release notes if we revert.
infra-bot: reserved tests complete: reproduced on pool-3, P99 delta matches local runs.
sam: pushed a WIP coalescing diff: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pulls/842 — needs review.
mika: closing loop — we'll aim to ship mitigation by EOD tomorrow if PR reviews go smoothly. thanks all.
